title: An Algebraic Structure for the Central Mexican Ritual Calendar
summary: This article develops an algebraic model of the 260-day Central Mexican ritual calendar, the \textit{Tonalpohualli}. We represent the calendar as the cyclic group $\mathbb{Z}_{13}\oplus\mathbb{Z}_{20}$, where each day name is encoded by a numeral-sign pair. From this model, we derive explicit correspondences between day numbers and day names through group actions. We also characterize, in algebraic terms, the twenty 13-day periods, the thirteen 20-day periods, and the partition of days into oriented tetrads.
